stated_mechanism: Guggulu inhibits platelet aggregation; with an anticoagulant or antiplatelet the bleeding risk rises.
Antiplatelet activity at therapeutic doses adds to the medicine's effect — the INR or bleeding time should be checked after starting.
Ginger and garlic inhibit platelets; small amounts in a compound are usually tolerated, but report any bruising or bleeding.

Glycyrrhizin causes potassium loss and sodium retention (pseudo-aldosteronism). Low potassium provokes digoxin toxicity, adds to a diuretic's potassium loss, and liquorice slows the clearance of corticosteroids.
Liquorice retains sodium and raises blood pressure against the medicine.
Diuretic herbs reduce lithium clearance; lithium rises toward toxic levels.
Additive diuresis — dehydration and electrolyte loss. Monitor weight and potassium.
Shankhpushpi lowers phenytoin blood levels (documented interaction); seizure control can be lost.
Additive CNS depression with benzodiazepines and other sedatives — drowsiness, slowed breathing, falls.
Reserpine depletes monoamines: it causes depression, worsens parkinsonism and adds to blood-pressure medicines.
Thyroid-active herbs change the thyroxine requirement — thyroid function should be rechecked at six weeks.
Piperine inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein and raises tacrolimus and cyclosporine levels toward toxicity.
Immunostimulant herbs work against an immunosuppressant; the prescriber should know.

stated_mechanism: Additive glucose lowering — check blood sugar more often and carry glucose.
Arishtas and Asavas contain self-generated alcohol; with metronidazole or disulfiram it causes a disulfiram reaction — flushing, vomiting, palpitations.
The alcohol in an Arishta or Asava adds to a sedative.
Purgation loses potassium and water, which raises digoxin and lithium toxicity and adds to a diuretic.
Avalehas, Gulams and Khandas are prepared in sugar or jaggery — often half the preparation by weight.
Arishtas and Asavas are fermented from jaggery and keep residual sugar; check blood glucose after starting.

stated_mechanism: Self-generated alcohol (typically 5-10%) in a liver that is already diseased. Kumaryasava is classically a liver medicine — contested; see the packet.
Alcohol relaxes the lower oesophageal sphincter and irritates the gastric lining.

Alcohol with a sleeping or sedating medicine in an older adult — the combination the Beers criteria list as a cause of falls and confusion.
Self-generated alcohol at an adult dose; withheld unless a Vaidya sets the dose.
